church.structure_note: A church is architecturally parallel to hoa_poa.json and condo_association.json -- it typically incorporates as a Texas nonprofit corporation (Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Chapter 22, same baseline as nonprofit.json) but has genuinely distinct content dense enough to warrant its own entity_type file rather than being folded into nonprofit.json as another industry layer. CONFIRMED 2026-09-04 (multiple independent sources): churches receive materially different, MORE FAVORABLE federal tax treatment than an ordinary 501(c)(3) nonprofit -- (1) IRC Section 508(c)(1)(A) makes a qualifying church automatically tax-exempt from the moment it is organized, with NO Form 1023/1023-EZ application required at all, unlike every other nonprofit in this dataset; (2) IRC Section 6033(a)(3)(A)(i) exempts churches, integrated auxiliaries, and conventions/associations of churches from the Form 990 annual filing requirement entirely -- critically, this means the automatic-revocation risk built into nonprofit.json's federal_tax_exemption_conditional category does NOT apply to a genuine church, since there is no required return to fail to file; (3) IRC Section 7611 imposes special procedural safeguards (higher-level IRS authorization, specific notice requirements) before the IRS may even examine a church's records -- no equivalent protection exists for an ordinary nonprofit. Two things still apply with NO exception: UBIT/Form 990-T if unrelated business income reaches $1,000 (churches get an ADDITIONAL $1,000 deduction per local unit within a convention or association of churches -- a genuine, distinctive wrinkle), and IRC Section 4958 excess benefit transaction/intermediate sanctions rules for insider dealings -- churches are NOT exempt from either. A REAL TRAP: this automatic exemption belongs to the church itself and does NOT extend to affiliated organizations operating as separate entities alongside it (thrift stores, schools, camps, outreach ministries) -- each of those needs its own recognition if it wants exemption. The IRS applies a multi-factor test (Publication 1828, no single factor determinative) to confirm an organization genuinely functions as a church before this special treatment applies -- self-designation alone is not sufficient. This file holds the GENERIC, denomination-agnostic baseline (formation, general clergy/governance structure, generic sacramental-recordkeeping categories); genuinely distinct polity and sacramental content by denomination (Catholic, Baptist, Episcopal, etc.) belongs in separate industry_church_{denomination}.json files layered on top, not duplicated here.

identity: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Status
Initial Governing Body Roster (Board/Elders/Deacons/Vestry, denomination-specific naming)
financial: CPA Review / Audit Reports (voluntary, not required)
Noncash Donation Appraisal Records (property gifts over $5,000)
statutory: Texas Business Organizations Code Chapter 22 Compliance
Foreign Qualification Filings (if operating in other states)
federal_tax_exempt_status: Church Tax Status Determination (Multi-Factor Test Documentation)
IRS Determination Letter (voluntary -- not required to be tax-exempt)
Unrelated Business Income Tax Records (Form 990-T, if applicable)
Excess Benefit Transaction / Intermediate Sanctions Compliance Records
Affiliated Organization Exemption Tracking (schools, thrift stores, camps operating as separate entities)
records_transparency: Document Retention Schedule (sacramental records commonly retained permanently in several traditions -- see denomination-specific industry file)

Certificate of Formation (Nonprofit Corp: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 22.001(5) -- same nonprofit-corporation formation basis as nonprofit.json. Most Texas churches incorporate this way, though a church is not legally required to incorporate to exist or to receive the federal tax treatment described in this file's structure_note.
Church Tax Status Determination (Multi-F: IRS Publication 1828 (Tax Guide for Churches and Religious Organizations) -- the IRS applies a multi-factor test to confirm an organization genuinely functions as a church (no single factor is determinative). CONFIRMED 2026-09-04 that such a test exists and governs eligibility for the special church tax rules; the specific enumerated factors were not independently verified in this research pass -- do not assert a specific list of factors as confirmed until a dedicated verification pass is done.
IRS Determination Letter (voluntary -- n: IRC Section 508(c)(1)(A) -- CONFIRMED 2026-09-04 across multiple independent sources: a qualifying church is automatically tax-exempt from the moment it is organized, with no Form 1023/1023-EZ filing required. Many churches still voluntarily seek a determination letter for donor confidence and banking purposes, but per IRS Publication 1828, donors may deduct contributions to a church even without one.
Unrelated Business Income Tax Records (F: IRC Sections 511-514, same $1,000 gross-income threshold and 21% flat rate as nonprofit.json's version of this citation. CONFIRMED 2026-09-04: churches receive an ADDITIONAL $1,000 deduction per local unit within a convention or association of churches -- a genuine wrinkle not present for an ordinary nonprofit.
Excess Benefit Transaction / Intermediat: IRC Section 4958 -- CONFIRMED 2026-09-04: churches are NOT exempt from these rules despite the broader Form 990/Form 1023 exemptions. Same disqualified-person and organization-manager penalty structure as nonprofit.json's version of this citation applies here without modification.
Noncash Donation Appraisal & Form 8283/8: CONFIRMED 2026-09-04: property donations (other than cash or publicly traded securities) worth more than $5,000 require a qualified independent appraisal and Form 8283 -- the church cannot serve as its own appraiser, and an authorized church official must sign Part V acknowledging receipt. If the church disposes of the property within 3 years, it must file Form 8282 within 125 days and send a copy to the donor.
Affiliated Organization Exemption Tracki: CONFIRMED 2026-09-04: the church's own automatic Section 508(c)(1)(A)/Section 6033(a)(3) exemption does NOT automatically extend to affiliated ministries, thrift stores, schools, or camps operating as legally separate organizations -- each must obtain its own recognition if exemption is desired. A real, commonly-missed compliance gap.
Clergy Housing Allowance Documentation: IRC Section 107 -- the parsonage/housing allowance exclusion for ministers, a well-established and longstanding provision. Note (not independently re-verified in this specific research pass, based on well-established general knowledge): clergy are commonly treated as employees for federal income tax withholding purposes but as self-employed for Social Security/Medicare (SECA) tax purposes -- a dual-status arrangement genuinely unique to clergy compensation. Flag for a dedicated verification pass if this needs the same primary-source confirmation standard as the rest of this file.
Workers' Compensation Policy: Tex. Labor Code Section 406.002 -- Texas is the only state in the country where workers' compensation coverage is elective, not mandatory, for most private employers. An employer who opts out ('non-subscriber') must notify the Texas Division of Workers' Compensation (Section 406.004) and notify employees (Section 406.005), and forfeits certain common-law defenses in the event of a workplace injury lawsuit. EXCEPTION: coverage is mandatory for government building/construction contracts under Section 406.096. Same citation already confirmed across every other entity file in this dataset.
